entities.summary:
Aimé-Marie-Gaspard de Clermont-Tonnerre (1779–1865), duc de Clermont-Tonnerre, was a French general and Restoration statesman from an ancient Dauphiné noble house. A veteran of Revolutionary and Napoleonic service who reintegrated into Bourbon politics, he held senior ministerial office under Louis XVIII and Charles X, notably as minister of war and of the navy in the 1820s.

His career tracks the path of aristocratic soldiers who survived regime change by offering administrative competence to successive monarchies. Ultra and moderate royalist currents both claimed such men as guarantors of order after 1815.

Clermont-Tonnerre embodies the Restoration’s attempt to fuse Napoleonic military professionalism with Bourbon legitimacy.
